title: Psychosocial predictors of fake news exposure and diffusion in Costa Rica (Predictores psicosociales de la exposicion y difusion de noticias falsas en Costa Rica)
screen_reason: Nationally representative survey of 805 Costa Rican adults reporting the share who say they shared news they considered false, separately for social media (19%) and WhatsApp (18%). These are self-reported SHARING shares with a stated denominator, i.e. RECALL (sharing). The paper's exposure measures are 5-point frequency scale MEANS only, with no share of respondents, so they yield no rows.

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who say they have shared news they considered false on social media
estimates.value_raw: 19% si / 81% no ("En el caso de redes sociales, 81% afirmo no haberlo hecho y 19%, si.")
estimates.denominator: 805 Costa Rican adults aged 18+ with Costa Rican nationality who own a mobile phone, random stratified national sample drawn from the SUTEL national numbering plan
estimates.definition: Answered 'yes' to a direct dichotomous (yes/no) question asking whether they had shared news they themselves considered false, on social media
estimates.misinfo_def: "Una noticia debe considerarse como falsa si, primero, posee un bajo nivel de facticidad... Una segunda caracteristica es que imitan la forma del contenido de las noticias periodisticas... Una tercera caracteristica es que son creadas desde motivaciones politicas, ideologicas o financieras para enganar deliberadamente a una audiencia." [English translation: "A news item should be considered false if, first, it has a low level of facticity... A second characteristic is that they imitate the form of journalistic news content... A third characteristic is that they are created from political, ideological or financial motivations in order to deliberately deceive an audience."]
estimates.source_quote: En el caso de redes sociales, 81% afirmó no haberlo hecho y 19%, sí.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: No external ground truth: the respondent's own judgement that the news item was false ('noticias que consideraban falsas'), captured by a single dichotomous yes/no item. No reliability statistic applies to this single item; Cronbach alphas are reported only for the predictor scales.
estimates.moderator_quote: Se indago si las personas compartieron noticias que consideraban falsas. Para ello, se consulto directamente si se habian compartido noticias de este tipo en redes sociales o por WhatsApp. Se utilizo una respuesta dicotomica, si/no.
estimates.notes: The paper does not state a reduced denominator for this item, so I take the full achieved sample of n=805 (the regression models run on 693-707 cases because of missing data on predictors, not because the sharing item was asked of a subset). Sample skews female (67%). English translation of the source quote: "In the case of social media, 81% said they had not done so and 19% said they had." The preceding sentence reads: "También se preguntó si las personas compartieron noticias que consideraban falsas." ["We also asked whether people had shared news they considered false."]

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who say they have shared news they considered false via WhatsApp
estimates.value_raw: 18% compartio / 82% no ("18% compartio noticias falsas y 82% afirmo que no")
estimates.denominator: 805 Costa Rican adults aged 18+ with Costa Rican nationality who own a mobile phone, random stratified national sample drawn from the SUTEL national numbering plan
estimates.definition: Answered 'yes' to a direct dichotomous (yes/no) question asking whether they had shared news they themselves considered false, via WhatsApp
estimates.misinfo_def: "Una noticia debe considerarse como falsa si, primero, posee un bajo nivel de facticidad... imitan la forma del contenido de las noticias periodisticas... son creadas desde motivaciones politicas, ideologicas o financieras para enganar deliberadamente a una audiencia." [English translation: "A news item should be considered false if, first, it has a low level of facticity... they imitate the form of journalistic news content... they are created from political, ideological or financial motivations in order to deliberately deceive an audience."]
estimates.source_quote: en el caso de WhatsApp: 18% compartió noticias falsas
estimates.ground_truth_detail: No external ground truth: the respondent's own judgement that the news item was false, captured by a single dichotomous yes/no item.
estimates.moderator_quote: Se indago si las personas compartieron noticias que consideraban falsas. Para ello, se consulto directamente si se habian compartido noticias de este tipo en redes sociales o por WhatsApp. Se utilizo una respuesta dicotomica, si/no.
estimates.notes: Separate row from the social-media figure because the paper reports the two platforms separately (and models them as two dependent variables, CNFRS and CNFW). English translation of the source quote: "in the case of WhatsApp: 18% shared fake news"; the full sentence is "El número es casi idéntico en el caso de WhatsApp: 18% compartió noticias falsas y 82% afirmó que no." ["The number is almost identical for WhatsApp: 18% shared fake news and 82% said they had not."]

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (1) Fake-news EXPOSURE is reported only as means on a 1-5 frequency scale -- social media M=3.02 (SD=1.18), news media M=2.96 (SD=1.12), WhatsApp M=2.90 (SD=1.25). No share of respondents above a threshold and no share reporting 'any' is given anywhere, so under the scale-means exclusion no exposure row is derivable. This is the paper's headline exposure measure, so an adjudicator should expect zero EXPOSURE/RECALL-exposure rows here. (2) '36% de la muestra afirmo tener mucha o demasiada capacidad para reconocer las noticias falsas' ['36% of the sample said they had a lot or too much capacity to recognise fake news'] -- this is self-perceived detection ability, not encountering or sharing misinformation, so out of scope. (3) 'la probabilidad de difundir noticias falsas en redes sociales se mantuvo en 54% para las personas con altos puntajes en autoritarismo (RM=1,17, p<,05)' -- a model-derived predicted probability for a predictor subgroup from a logistic model the authors themselves describe as non-significant at all three levels; not a descriptive prevalence, so not a row. (4) Regression coefficients in Tables 1 and 2 are associations, not shares.

rob.design: Cross-sectional national telephone survey. Random stratified sampling with the SUTEL national mobile numbering plan as the frame; inclusion criteria 18+ and Costa Rican nationality; fielded 13-19 May 2019 in morning, afternoon and evening slots; quotas maintained on province, sex and age against the 2017 national statistics, and the education variable weighted to balance primary and secondary levels. n=805; 67% women; age 18-88 (M=38.83, SD=15.75); education 42% primary, 37% secondary, 21% university. Stated sampling error +/-3.45 percentage points at 95% confidence. NO RESPONSE RATE OR COOPERATION RATE IS REPORTED. Measures: exposure and self-perceived recognition on 5-point frequency scales (never-always); sharing as a single dichotomous yes/no item. Reliability reported only for predictor scales (RWA alpha=.79; social dominance .66/.68; animadversion .91; need for cognition .54; need to evaluate .59). No external verification of what respondents counted as false.
rob.item6_quote: Una noticia debe considerarse como falsa si, primero, posee un bajo nivel de facticidad. Es decir, aunque una noticia falsa tenga informacion correcta, la mayoria de su contenido es fabricado o falso (Tandoc et al., 2018). [English translation: "A news item should be considered false if, first, it has a low level of facticity. That is, even though a fake news item may contain correct information, most of its content is fabricated or false."]
rob.item10_quote: En el caso de redes sociales, 81% afirmo no haberlo hecho y 19%, si. El numero es casi identico en el caso de WhatsApp: 18% compartio noticias falsas y 82% afirmo que no. [English translation: "In the case of social media, 81% said they had not done so and 19% said they had. The number is almost identical for WhatsApp: 18% shared fake news and 82% said they had not."]
